record.paper_title: Pole solutions in the case of problems of flame front propagation and Saffman-Teylor "finger" formation without surface tension: open problems and possible ways of their solutions
record.context_brief: Distribution of allowed initial conditions over α
record.original_question: For the general pole solution in zero-surface-tension Saffman-Taylor channel growth, let the real parameter α be the sum of the complex pole parameters α_i, and let the asymptotic finger thickness be 1 − α/2, so that α = 1 corresponds to a finger of half the channel width and 0 < α < 2 corresponds to physically possible finger thicknesses between 0 and 1. As a function of α in the interval 0 < α < 2, what fraction of all possible initial pole configurations with that α are allowed rather than singular, and does this α-dependent distribution support selection of the half-width finger as the most probable asymptotic outcome?

evidence.quote: The general pole solution (5) in work [3] is characterized by the real parameter α being the sum of the complex parameters αi for poles. Thickness of the asymptotic finger is simple function of α: (Thickness = 1 − α/2). The value (α = 1) corresponds to thickness 1/2. As far as possible thickness of the "finger" is between 0 and 1, possible α value is in an interval between 0 and 2: (0 < α < 2).

How number of these "allowed" initial pole conditions (to be exact speaking, their percent from the full number of the possible initial pole conditions corresponding to the given real value α) is distributed inside of this interval?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Saffman–Taylor problem of a viscous finger advancing in a Hele-Shaw channel of unit width in the absence of surface tension. The interface admits an exact family of pole solutions, parameterized by a finite collection of complex pole locations together with their (complex) strengths α_i. For such a configuration define the real parameter
   α = Σ_i α_i ∈ ℝ,
and recall that the corresponding asymptotic finger has thickness 1 − α/2; thus physically meaningful finger widths between 0 and 1 correspond to α ∈ (0, 2), with α = 1 yielding the half-channel-width finger.

Call an initial pole configuration "allowed" if its dynamical evolution under the zero-surface-tension Saffman–Taylor pole equations remains regular for all positive times (does not develop a finite-time singularity of the pole system before the finger forms), and call it "singular" otherwise.

For each α ∈ (0, 2), let ρ(α) denote the fraction (relative measure, with respect to a natural parameterization of all pole configurations whose strengths sum to α) of allowed initial pole configurations among all possible initial pole configurations with that prescribed value of α.

Problem.
(a) Determine the function ρ : (0, 2) → [0, 1].
(b) Decide whether ρ(α) is peaked (or otherwise distinguished) at α = 1, in such a way that the half-channel-width finger emerges as the most probable asymptotic outcome of a generic admissible initial pole configuration.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals an extensive literature on Saffman–Taylor finger selection (Combescot–Hakim–Pomeau, Tanveer, Magdaleno–Casademunt, and rigorous work on kinetic-undercooling selection) and on pole dynamics in zero-surface-tension Laplacian growth, but none of the located sources address the specific question of the measure-theoretic distribution ρ(α) of allowed versus singular initial pole configurations as a function of the total pole-strength parameter α, nor establish that this distribution selects the half-width finger as most probable. The status of this specific selection-by-initial-condition-measure question therefore appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Selection of the Saffman-Taylor Finger Width in the Absence of Surface Tension: An Exact Result
status_evidence.snippet: Studies pole dynamics and selection mechanisms but addresses ε→0 surface-tension selection rather than measure of allowed pole initial conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Related selection results exist but not for ρ(α) of pole initial conditions.

status_evidence.title: Rigorous results in existence and selection of Saffman–Taylor fingers by kinetic undercooling
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous selection results in presence of kinetic undercooling regularization.
status_evidence.claim: Selection in zero-surface-tension limit via pole-configuration measure is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Laplacian Growth II: Saffman–Taylor Problem Without Surface Tension
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses formation of one finger with half of the channel width via pole dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Related physical context but does not compute fraction of allowed initial pole configurations as function of α.
